content_voiceover: This is the complement cascade slide, and you need to know exactly where each PNH drug acts. Complement can be activated through three pathways, classical, lectin, or alternative, and all three converge on C3 convertase. The alternative pathway is constitutively active, ticking over C3 to C3b, which is why PNH red cells, lacking the protective proteins CD55 and CD59, are especially vulnerable. In the proximal pathway, Iptacopan inhibits Factor B and Danicopan inhibits Factor D, both blocking formation of the C3 convertase from the alternative pathway side. CD55, the protein missing in PNH, normally accelerates decay of that convertase. Pegcetacoplan inhibits C3 itself, blocking cleavage into C3a and C3b, which shuts down both the proximal amplification loop and downstream C5 convertase formation. Moving to the terminal pathway, C5 is cleaved into C5a and C5b, and C5b combines with C6 through C9 to form the membrane attack complex, which is what CD59 normally blocks. The terminal C5 inhibitors, eculizumab, ravulizumab, and crovalimab, all block this step, preventing intravascular hemolysis but not extravascular hemolysis, since C3b opsonization upstream is untouched. Investigational agents target MASP-3, Factor D, Factor H, and C3 as well.
keypoints: C5 inhibitors (eculizumab/ravulizumab/crovalimab) block MAC, mimic CD59
C3/proximal inhibitors (pegcetacoplan, iptacopan, danicopan) block upstream, mimic CD55/CFB/CFD
C5 inhibitors stop IVH but not EVH (C3b opsonization persists)
Alternative pathway is constitutively active — why PNH RBCs are vulnerable
Proximal inhibition addresses breakthrough EVH on C5 inhibitors
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, map the drugs to their targets. Terminal C5 inhibitors, eculizumab, ravulizumab, and crovalimab, block the membrane attack complex, essentially replacing the function of CD59, and they control intravascular hemolysis but not extravascular hemolysis. Proximal inhibitors act further upstream, iptacopan blocks Factor B, danicopan blocks Factor D, and pegcetacoplan blocks C3 directly, replacing the function of CD55. These proximal agents control both intravascular and extravascular hemolysis, which matters clinically for patients with breakthrough extravascular hemolysis while on a C5 inhibitor.
